bull.argument: NIKE's filing shows a company with durable economics that is working through a deliberate reset. Fiscal 2026 revenue was $46.4 billion, roughly flat, and gross margin widened 20 basis points to 42.9%. North America, the largest segment, grew 5% currency-neutral with EBIT up 14% to $5.4 billion, showing the core franchise still converts demand into profit. The company also recovered $986 million of IEEPA tariffs, with substantially all of the remaining receivable collected after year end. The balance sheet supports the reset: $9.0 billion in cash and short-term investments, an A+/A2 long-term rating, and an ROIC of 18.7%. Management is also cutting the weakest exposures, with Greater China and Converse expected to weigh through fiscal 2027 and actions targeted for completion by December 2026. The risks are real, and the filing says so, but the bull case rests on a strong brand and cash-generating core being repositioned, not broken.

claims.claim: North America grew and expanded margins, showing the core franchise is still profitable.
claims.quote: North America revenues increased 5% on a currency-neutral basis.

claims.claim: The company recovered a large IEEPA tariff benefit that offset tariff costs in fiscal 2026.
claims.quote: we recognized a benefit of $986 million in Cost of sales within the Consolidated Statements of Income for the recovery of IEEPA tariffs paid

claims.claim: The balance sheet and liquidity remain strong, with investment-grade ratings and substantial cash.
claims.quote: We currently have long-term debt ratings of A+ and A2 from S&P Global Ratings and Moody's Ratings, respectively.

bear.argument: The bull case leans on headline figures that the filing itself qualifies. Net income fell 3% to $3.1 billion and EBIT margin was 8.3%, down from 12.7% two years earlier. Fiscal 2026 gross profit was lifted by a $986 million IEEPA tariff recovery, a one-time item that largely offset tariffs recognized in the same year, so the reported 20 basis point gross margin gain is not evidence of durable economics. NIKE Brand Digital sales fell 12%, Greater China revenue fell 13% currency-neutral with EBIT down 20%, and Converse EBIT collapsed 93% to $18 million. Management expects negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue through fiscal 2027, and it recorded $385 million in severance with more charges possible. Operating cash flow fell to $2.9 billion from $3.7 billion, and the company paused buybacks. The filing also states that management may not realize a satisfactory return on NIKE Direct investments.

claims.claim: Reported gross margin gain was helped by a one-time tariff recovery, not purely operations.
claims.quote: we recognized a benefit of $986 million in Cost of sales within the Consolidated Statements of Income for the recovery of IEEPA tariffs paid

claims.claim: Management expects weakness in Greater China and Converse to persist into fiscal 2027.
claims.quote: We expect negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue throughout fiscal 2027.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow declined and the company paused share repurchases.
claims.quote: We paused repurchases under this program during the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and no shares were repurchased during the quarter ended May 31, 2026.

bull.argument: I concede the points the filing clearly supports. The $986 million IEEPA recovery flatters fiscal 2026 gross margin, so the 20 basis point gain is not evidence of durable improvement. Greater China, Converse and NIKE Brand Digital are weak, and the filing warns that NIKE Direct returns may disappoint. My case is narrower. North America is the profit engine: revenue rose 5% currency-neutral and segment EBIT rose 14% to $5.4 billion, so the core franchise still converts demand into earnings. The cash decline is partly timing, since the filing says substantially all of the remaining IEEPA receivable was collected after year end. Liquidity is ample at $9.0 billion of cash and short-term investments, and the company has no borrowings under its commercial paper program. The bull case therefore depends on the North America franchise funding a reset of the weaker segments, not on the headline margin. That is a more modest claim, but the filing supports it.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow was depressed partly by timing, because the IEEPA receivable was collected after year end.
claims.quote: Subsequent to May 31, 2026, we received substantially all of the remaining IEEPA tariff receivable.

claims.claim: North America, the largest segment, grew EBIT 14% on higher reported revenues.
claims.quote: Reported EBIT increased 14% reflecting higher reported revenues and the following:

claims.claim: Liquidity is substantial, with $9.0 billion of cash and short-term investments.
claims.quote: As of May 31, 2026, we had Cash and equivalents and Short-term investments totaling $9.0 billion

bear.argument: The opponent has conceded the key weaknesses, but the North America case is weaker than it looks. North America's EBIT gain was helped by a $965 million share of the IEEPA recovery, which largely offset tariffs recognized in fiscal 2026. Strip that out and the segment's profit story depends on a one-time item, not franchise economics. North America's wholesale revenue rose 14%, but NIKE Direct fell 6% and North America digital sales fell 10%, so the segment's growth is partly a shift into wholesale, where the filing admits lower ASP from channel mix. The cash argument also cuts both ways: the filing says operating cash flow fell to $2,868 million from $3,698 million even after the IEEPA receivable was partly collected, and the working capital drag was $1,678 million. Liquidity of $9.0 billion is real, but it is down from prior levels and the company funded $2.3 billion of dividends from it. Finally, the filing says the actions are not expected to finish until December 2026, and it warns that more severance charges may follow. A reset funded by a single segment whose profit is flattered by a one-time recovery is a risky bet.

claims.claim: North America's EBIT gain was helped by a large share of the one-time IEEPA recovery.
claims.quote: $965 million and $21 million of the benefit was classified within North America and Converse, respectively

claims.claim: North America's direct-to-consumer business declined, with digital sales down 10%.
claims.quote: NIKE Direct revenues decreased 6% due to declines in digital sales of 10% and declines in store sales of 2%.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow fell sharply year over year despite the recovery.
claims.quote: cash provided by operations was $2,868 million. This was driven by Net income of $3,108 million

judge.reasoning: All of the bear's quotes verified and it directly tied the IEEPA recovery to North America's EBIT gain, which undercuts the bull's central claim. The bull conceded the headline weaknesses and narrowed its case to North America, but it did not answer the $965 million recovery point with an ex-recovery figure, and its cash-timing argument is weakened by the bear's point that operating cash flow fell even after partial collection.
